read_by: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and decision log
input: FSim conditional flame-length class state, exact integer 0 to 6 (0 = no event); nothing between classes
out_of_scope: Contents (declared as a withheld placeholder part)
Smoke, soot and ash without fire damage

how_to_use.share_of: Structure replacement cost new of the same building

outputs.single_event: conditional: proposal, not in the runtime index; building and FSim product required
outputs.scenario_dollars: withheld until the building value is qualified
outputs.yearly_loss: withheld before promotion (computed by the consumer afterwards)

conditions: Fractional or out-of-range classes are rejected; a burn probability in the damage call is rejected

method.summary: US Forest Service home loss by flame-length class (shrub vegetation) for the house; warehouse 0.8x and office 0.9x from same-fire CAL FIRE inspection ratios

key_sources: USFS, Wildfire Risk to Communities spatial datasets, 2nd ed. (2024) (WFRE-S001)
FEMA National Risk Index, Dec 2025 (WFRE-S006; check only)
judgment: Forest Service loss figure read as repair cost / rebuild cost
Shrub vegetation used everywhere (tree and grass as sensitivity)
Forest Service 30 m classes treated as the same as Hazard's 270 m FSim classes
One building factor at every class

checks.name: FEMA National Risk Index: yearly loss on Hazard's grid
CAL FIRE inspections: building-type outcomes inside the same fires

open_items: Hazard's fire rate is the wildland rate, not where buildings sit (East reads higher against NRI)
Hazard's generic loader accepts a fractional class and a burn probability (two loader gaps)

rows.cost_basis: our reading of the loss figure as rebuild-cost share

rows.cost_basis: our reading of the loss figure as rebuild-cost share
